summary: Wilhelm Dilthey was a philosopher who studied at Heidelberg University and Humboldt University of Berlin. He held academic posts at the University of Basel (~1866–1868), Kiel University (~1868–1871), University of Breslau (~1871–1882), and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1882–1905).
Wilhelm Eggers specialized in Indology. He studied at the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology, the German Colonial School, and Kiel University, where he earned his Ph.D. under Friedrich Otto Schrader.
Wilhelm Ferdinand Hüttemann was an Indologist. In 1890, he studied under Ernst Leumann and earned his Ph.D. at the University of Strasbourg.

Wilhelm Filchner worked in Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at the Prussian Military Academy, Humboldt University of Berlin, University of Königsberg, and University of Munich, and became a professor at Humboldt University of Berlin in 1938.

Wilhelm Gampert was an Indologist who earned his Ph.D. at the German University in Prague, studying under Moriz Winternitz and Otto Stein. From 1945 to 1978, he served as a scientific worker at the Czech Academy of Sciences' Oriental Institute.

Wilhelm Geiger was an Indologist, linguist, and scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Erlangen-Nuremberg, Bonn, and Berlin, later holding posts at Neustadt, Maximiliansgymnasium München, University of Erlangen-Nuremberg, and University of Munich (Professor 1920–1924).

Wilhelm Germann worked in Indology, religious studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg from ~1860 to 1864 and held a post with the Leipzig Evangelical Lutheran Mission in 1864.

Wilhelm Gesenius worked in linguistics and religious studies. He studied at the University of Helmstedt and University of Göttingen under Thomas Christian Tychsen. He held posts at Göttingen (~1806–1810) and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1810–1842).

Wilhelm Grube was a sinologist and linguist who studied at Saint Petersburg and Leipzig. He worked at the Asiatic Museum, Berlin's Ethnological Museum, and taught at the University of Leipzig before becoming extraordinary professor at Humboldt University of Berlin in 1892.
Wilhelm Gundert was a scholar of Japanology and religious studies who succeeded Karl Florenz. He held a post at the University of Hamburg from ~1936 to 1945.

Wilhelm Halbfass was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at Vienna, Göttingen (under Ernst Waldschmidt), and Hamburg. His career included posts at Göttingen, Brock University, and the University of Pennsylvania, where he became professor in 1982.

Wilhelm Havers was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Tübingen, Leipzig, and Berlin. He held posts at Strasbourg, Leipzig, Bern (ord. Professor 1915), Würzburg (Professor 1920), Breslau (Professor 1929), and Vienna (Professor 1937–1953).

Wilhelm Jahn specialized in Indology. He studied at Berlin, Marburg, Rostock, Kiel, Leipzig, and Würzburg, earning his Ph.D. under Julius Jolly. He held posts as Privatdozent at the University of Zurich (1909–1918) and taught at Halle-Wittenberg (1918–1919).

Wilhelm K. Essler is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied at the University of Munich under Wolfgang Stegmüller and Wilhelm Britzelmayr. He served as Director of the Institute for Philosophy at Goethe University Frankfurt from ~1978 to 2005.

Wilhelm Koppers was a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at Missionshaus St. Gabriel and the University of Vienna, where he completed his Ph.D. He later served as Privatdozent and Professor/Director at the University of Vienna.

Wilhelm Krause worked in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Vienna and Graz. After teaching at high schools, he was appointed lecturer in Sanskrit (1960) and extraordinary professor (1968) at the University of Graz.

Wilhelm Max Müller was a scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and the University of Leipzig, and later held a post at the University of Pennsylvania from ~1909 to 1919.

Wilhelm Pertsch was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and Tübingen under Franz Bopp, Albrecht Weber, and Rudolf von Roth. He served as librarian at Forschungsbibliothek Gotha and director of Schloss Friedenstein's scientific institutions.

Wilhelm Printz was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Leipzig, Göttingen, Berlin (Ph.D. under Heinrich Lüders), and Frankfurt. He held posts at Frankfurt, the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft, and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (ao. Professor 1929–1939).

Wilhelm Rau was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Leipzig and Marburg, earning his Ph.D. under Johannes Nobel. He served as a professor at Goethe University Frankfurt (1955) and Ordinarius at the University of Marburg from 1957 to 1988.
